title: 第584章 风传暗语人心半寸寒第583章 阴棋落地人心有隙亦有光
slug: 喵仙宗主从猫薄荷开始证道长生
content_zh:
晨光是软的。
人心是脆的。
归仙峰的天光依旧澄澈，洗得山林青翠、殿宇明净，半点看不出暗流潜行。山风掠过青石阶，卷着淡淡的灵草香与丹药暖雾，四堂修士各司其职，步履安稳，烟火与道韵相融，一派盛世宗门光景。
外人看在眼里，是新生正道蒸蒸日上，万众归心，牢不可破。
只有林墨知道，最狠的从不是刀兵相向的厮杀。
是无声渗透的猜忌。
是藏在热忱底下的犹疑。
是明明身在光明，心底却莫名生出一缕寒凉，说不清、道不明、斩不断、除不尽。
胖橘慵懒地蜷在主峰殿门前的白玉石台之上，橘毛蓬松柔软，被晨光晒得暖融融的。
看上去，它在打盹。
四爪收拢，长尾轻搭身侧，眼皮半耷，呼吸均匀，活脱脱一副贪睡懒猫模样。
可若有神识极致通透者细细探查，便能察觉，它周身萦绕的温润道韵从未停歇。
一缕缕、一丝丝，如风漫山，如水入脉，温柔裹住整座归仙峰。
不镇压，不根除，不暴戾驱邪。
只是轻轻抚平人心深处翻涌的细碎惶惑，一点点熨平蛊念滋生的细微裂痕。
上古猫仙道统，从来不用杀伐定乾坤。
只用温柔守本心。
林墨立在它身侧，白衣无尘，身姿挺拔。
他垂眸看着山下往来的修士，眼底无波澜，无轻视，无焦灼。
世人皆道，战胜伪天黑蛊，归仙峰便稳了。

可棋局从来不在地脉，不在蛊毒，不在山河阵法。
在人。
人心一寸裂，棋局千丈空。
风从山坳处吹来，带着初秋的微凉，掠过人群耳畔，悄无声息捎来了第一缕暗语。
最先乱的，从来不是修为高深、道心稳固的老牌修士。
是那些刚刚投奔归仙峰、半生漂泊、从未见过真正正道的底层散修。
他们的赤诚最真，他们的根基最浅。
他们敢拼命护光明，也最容易被一丝风吹草动动摇心神。
山路边的青石板上，两个刚入宗不久的低阶修士并肩清扫落叶，手里的竹帚轻轻扫过满地碎光，声音压得极低，带着难以掩饰的迟疑。
“你昨夜……真真切切看清黑蛊被除了？”
问话的少年指尖死死攥着竹帚柄，指腹磨着粗糙的竹纹，微微发紧。他说话时眼皮微垂，不敢转头看身旁同伴，像是怕从对方眼里看见自己心底的怯懦。
另一人愣了愣，停下手里动作，下意识摸了摸自己的后颈，那是他紧张时改不掉的习惯。
“那还能有假？猫仙尊一声鸣，地脉黑气尽数消散，全山修士都亲眼所见，哪能有诈？”
“可我方才听外山的游修闲聊，说……那黑蛊根本没断根。”
前一句声音还稳，后一句落下，已然带上了发颤的轻气。
短短一句话，像一粒细沙，轻轻落进平静的湖面。
不起大浪，只起微澜。
“瞎说！”后者当即蹙眉，语气硬撑着笃定，耳根却悄悄泛红，“咱归仙宗堂堂正道，林墨仙尊通天彻地，猫仙尊镇守地脉，岂能留此大患？纯属外人嚼舌根！”
content_en:
The morning light is soft.
The human heart is fragile.
The skylight at Guixian Peak is still clear, washing the mountains and forests green, making the palaces bright and clear, and there is no undercurrent at all. The mountain breeze swept over the bluestone steps, carrying the faint scent of spiritual herbs and the warm mist of elixirs. The monks in the four halls each performed their duties, walking steadily, and the fireworks and Taoist charms blended together, creating a scene of a prosperous sect.
In the eyes of outsiders, the new righteous path is flourishing, and the people are united in it, and it is unbreakable.
Only Lin Mo knew that the most cruel thing was never a fight with swords.
It's the suspicion that creeps in silently.
It is the hesitation hidden under the enthusiasm.
It is clear that I am in the light, but there is an inexplicable coldness in my heart. I can't explain it, I don't understand it, I can't cut it off, and I can't get rid of it.
Fat Orange curled up lazily on the white jade stone platform in front of the main peak hall. The orange hair was fluffy and soft, and was warmed by the morning sun.
It looked like it was taking a nap.
The four paws are folded, the long tail is lightly draped against the side, the eyelids are half drooped, and the cat is breathing evenly, looking like a sleepy and lazy cat.
But if someone with extremely penetrating spiritual consciousness examines it carefully, they will be able to notice that the warm Taoist charm lingering around it has never stopped.
Wisps and threads, like the wind flowing over the mountain, like water entering the veins, gently wrap around the entire Guixian Peak.
No suppression, no eradication, no violence to drive away evil spirits.
It just gently soothes the tiny confusions surging deep in people's hearts, and irons out the tiny cracks caused by the evil thoughts bit by bit.
In the ancient cat immortal tradition, there was never any need to kill to determine the universe.
Just keep your heart with gentleness.
Lin Mo stood beside it, dressed in white and dust-free, with a tall and straight posture.
He lowered his eyes and looked at the monks coming and going down the mountain. There was no wave, no contempt, no anxiety in his eyes.
Everyone knows that if you defeat the False Sky Black Gu, Guixian Peak will be stable.
But the chess game never lies in the earth's veins, poison, or mountain and river formations.
In people.
People's hearts are broken, and the chess game is completely empty.
The wind blew from the mountain col, carrying the coolness of early autumn, passing by the ears of the crowd, quietly carrying the first ray of code.
The first ones to cause chaos are never the veteran monks with advanced cultivation and stable Taoist hearts.
They are those low-level casual cultivators who have just defected to Guixian Peak, have been wandering for half their lives, and have never seen the true right path.
Their sincerity is the most genuine and their foundation is the shallowest.
They dare to protect the light with all their strength, but they are also the most easily shaken by the slightest disturbance.
On the bluestone slab on the roadside of the mountain, two low-level monks who had just joined the sect were cleaning fallen leaves side by side. The bamboo brooms in their hands gently swept the scattered light on the ground, their voices were very low, with an undisguised hesitation.
"You...really saw the black poison being removed last night?"
The fingertips of the young man who asked the question were tightly clenched on the bamboo broom handle, and the fingertips were rubbed against the rough bamboo lines, making them slightly tight. When he spoke, his eyelids drooped slightly, and he did not dare to turn his head to look at his companion, as if he was afraid of seeing the cowardice in his heart from the other person's eyes.
The other person was stunned, stopped what he was doing, and subconsciously touched the back of his neck. That was a habit he couldn't get rid of when he was nervous.
"How can it be false? When the Cat Immortal Lord screams, all the black energy in the earth's veins dissipates. All the monks in the mountain see it with their own eyes. How can there be any fraud?"
"But I just heard the wandering cultivator from the outer mountain chatting and said... that the black poison has not been cut off at all."
The voice of the first sentence was still steady, but the voice of the second sentence was already trembling with lightness.
A short sentence, like a grain of sand, gently falling into the calm lake.
There are no big waves, only small ripples.
"Nonsense!" The latter immediately frowned and spoke firmly, but his ears secretly turned red, "We return to the Immortal Sect in an upright way. Lin Mo Immortal Lord can penetrate the sky and the earth, and Cat Immortal Lord guards the earth. How can we leave such a big problem? It's just an outsider's gossip!"
